overview.headline: Mach number links speed of sound to density changes and compressibility

keyPoints.point: Mach number is ratio of aircraft speed to speed of sound
keyPoints.quote: The Mach number is the ratio of the speed of the aircraft, or the speed of the gas, to the speed of sound in the gas.

keyPoints.point: Low speed keeps air density constant but higher speed compresses air locally
keyPoints.quote: If the aircraft passes at a low speed, typically less than 250 mph, it is observed that the density of the air remains constant.

keyPoints.point: Subsonic Mach below one makes density change very small so compressibility can be ignored
keyPoints.quote: For low speed, or subsonic conditions, the Mach number is less than one, M < 1, and the square of the Mach number is very small.

keyPoints.point: Supersonic Mach above one makes density change faster than velocity by square of Mach number
keyPoints.quote: For supersonic and hypersonic flows, the density changes faster than the velocity changes by a factor equal to the square of the Mach number.

keyTerms.gloss: ratio that compares aircraft speed to speed of sound to assess compressibility effects
keyTerms.quote: The Mach number is the ratio of the speed of the aircraft, or the speed of the gas, to the speed of sound in the gas.

keyTerms.gloss: speed at which small disturbances travel isentropically through the gas
keyTerms.quote: where a is equal to the speed of sound.

keyTerms.gloss: effect that alters aerodynamic force when air density changes at higher speed
keyTerms.quote: This compressibility effect alters the amount of resulting force on the aircraft since the aerodynamic force depends on the air density.

keyTerms.gloss: air property that remains constant at low speed and varies when compressibility becomes important
keyTerms.quote: If the aircraft passes at a low speed, typically less than 250 mph, it is observed that the density of the air remains constant.

keyTerms.gloss: disturbances that affect lift and drag and change downstream flow conditions near speed of sound
keyTerms.quote: Sharp disturbances generate shock waves that affect both the lift and drag of the aircraft and the flow conditions downstream of the shock wave.
